To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of digital technologies by university students is low, with only 20-30% of students using any one technology; (2) students use a limited set of technologies, and use of collaborative knowledge creation and virtual world technologies was low; (3) the use of technology by 'digital natives' was not qualitatively different to 'digital immigrants'; and (4) students' use of technology was related to the nature of their course.

1) University students' technology use is more similar than it is different, regardless of their age, technical discipline or the extent to which they are digital natives; 2) Students' use of technology is not a radical departure from previous generations; and 3) Students' use is more influenced by their teachers' teaching styles and the requirements of their courses than by their age, technical background, or the extent to whic they are digital natives.
